findings.title: KeyError if `integration.metadata` lacks `sender` key
findings.body: The expression `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` will raise a `KeyError` (resulting in a 500 error) if the integration's metadata does not contain a `sender` key or if `sender` does not contain a `login` key. The `sender` field is only populated via webhook processing of the `installation` event. If the webhook was not received or processed (e.g., due to a timing issue, network failure, or if the integration was created through a different path), this line will crash instead of showing the user-friendly error page. Use `.get()` with a fallback or wrap in a try/except to handle this gracefully.

findings.title: Unhandled exception from `get_user_info` propagates as 500
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` makes an HTTP request to GitHub's API. If this call raises an exception (network timeout, GitHub API error, connection refused, etc.), the exception is unhandled and will bubble up as a 500 Internal Server Error instead of returning the user-friendly error page via `error()`. The surrounding code only checks whether `"login"` is in the returned dict, but doesn't protect against the call itself failing.

findings.title: `redirect_uri` is not URL-encoded in the OAuth authorize URL
findings.body: The `redirect_uri` value (e.g., `http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/`) is interpolated directly into the query string without percent-encoding. Characters like `:` and `/` in the redirect URI should be encoded per RFC 3986 for query parameter values. While many OAuth providers tolerate this, it can cause parsing issues with certain proxies or stricter implementations. Use `urllib.parse.urlencode` or `quote` to properly encode the parameters.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` actually tests state mismatch, not a 404 from GitHub
findings.body: The test uses `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` which does not match the pipeline signature (which is `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` based on other tests). This means the request fails at the state validation check (line 412 of integration.py) and never reaches the `get_installation_info` call that would return the mocked 404. The test passes but validates the wrong code path — it tests state mismatch rather than the installation-not-found scenario it claims to test.

findings.title: Missing `redirect_uri` in OAuth token exchange request
findings.body: The OAuth2 token exchange (lines 416-420) does not include the `redirect_uri` parameter, even though it was provided in the authorization request (line 408). Per RFC 6749 §4.1.3, `redirect_uri` is REQUIRED in the token request if it was included in the authorization request. While GitHub's implementation currently tolerates this omission, it violates the OAuth2 spec and could break if GitHub tightens validation. Include the same `redirect_uri` value in the token exchange data.
